subject: ADR-203: what has not left this device -- the outbox, a ledger and not a transport
body: The ask was Starlink. The honest version of it for a page opened off a card over file:// is NOT A DISH: a page cannot speak to a modem, a satellite or a server, and a component that pretended to would be a lie about DATA SAFETY, which is the most expensive kind. What a page CAN do -- and what nothing in this kit did -- is know precisely what is on this device and nowhere else, so a few minutes of signal go on the right bytes. So: A LEDGER, NOT A TRANSPORT, and the strip says so in the page rather than in a comment. KEEP says 'saved on this device' and immediately says it is not a backup; the outbox is the other half of that sentence. They share exactly ONE thing on purpose -- KEEP.wire now returns snapshot() (keep.py 1.1.0) and the outbox reads the sheet through it, because a second description of 'what is on this page' would be a second thing to keep in step and the one the outbox used would be the one nobody tested. THREE WAYS THE OBVIOUS VERSION IS WRONG. IT MARKS ON SUCCESS, NEVER ON CLICK: the hook is inside the clipboard promise's resolve path, because a ledger that stamped on the button would tell a reader their morning is safe when it is on no device but this one -- a wrong toast is forgotten in a second, a wrong ledger is read as reassurance a week later. IT IS PER EXPORT, NOT PER SHEET: one stamp for the sheet would go quiet about the Darwin Core the moment the CSV was copied, which is UNDER-REPORTING, the direction that loses data. AN EXPORT IT DOES NOT KNOW IS AN ERROR, NOT A SHRUG -- an undeclared id turns the strip red and NAMES THE STRING, which is what makes a mis-wired call site loud, the failure ADR-201 found the hard way when a typeof guard hid a wrong function name for a season. DECLARED AND COUNTED ARE TWO DIFFERENT LISTS: every copy a sheet can make is declared, including the AI prompt and the species pack that carry no records, or a call site could hand out bytes the ledger has never heard of; and only the ones that carry records are COUNTED, because an outbox that nagged you to re-copy a prompt every time you added a stem is an outbox nobody reads, and an outbox nobody reads is worse than none because the page still looks like it is keeping track. THE SHEET AS IT CAME OUT OF THE BOX IS NOT WORK -- three of these pages fill a date in for you, so the baseline is the state at wire time, UNLESS the autosave just restored something, in which case every export is genuinely outstanding: work that came back from the autosave has been on exactly one device, and greeting it with 'nothing on this sheet yet' would be the most expensive sentence in the kit. ONE CHECKSUM FOR THE KIT: FEK's CRC-32 over UTF-8 the outbox encodes itself, no second implementation and NO FALLBACK -- if FEK is absent it REFUSES and says it is tracking nothing -- and both are held to Python's str.encode and zlib.crc32 on a corpus with an accent, an em dash and a surrogate pair, because a hash that were merely self-consistent would report 'unchanged' on a sheet that had changed. WHAT DRIVING IT FOUND: document.execCommand('copy') REPORTS FAILURE BY RETURNING FALSE and throws in only some of the ways it can fail, and FIVE of the eight consumers ignored the return value in their clipboard fallback -- releve, the stand sheet, the collection sheet, the greenhouse and the pheno tracker all toasted 'Copied' over a copy the browser had refused. That fault predates this slice by a long way; the ledger is what made it visible. The check is written against EVERY consumer, driven through a real button with both clipboard paths refusing and, first, with both accepting, so the refusal check cannot pass for the boring reason that the button never copied anything at all. The pheno tracker also carried the clipboard dance twice, inline, the only sheet with no copyText of its own. IT IS OBSERVABLE WITH NO NEW PROTOCOL: the strip is role=status aria-live=polite, so what changes when an export lands reaches a screen reader and reaches the door through ADR-199's `said` and ADR-200's `any-contains`. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it never sends anything; it cannot know whether what left ARRIVED, so it claims 'left this device' and no more; and it OVER-REPORTS once, on purpose, because pending is computed on the whole sheet's state -- the safe direction, where closing it would mean declaring what each export reads, a list that would go out of date silently. verify_outbox is NEW at 188 checks, mutate_outbox NEW at 20 mutants all killed -- fifteen in the component and five in one page's wiring, because a fault in the component arrives on eight pages at once and a fault in the wiring arrives on one, silently. verify_emitters 130 -> 156.
